Message Performance

What we actually said, and which of it earned attention — 2025-11-14 to 2026-11-14
Last updated November 14, 2026 at 08:18 AM • refreshed daily by the analytics pipeline
Read this first. ROAS on this page is platform-attributed — Meta's and Google's own reported conversion value divided by spend. It is not Shopify truth and it is not incremental. Use it to rank pillars against each other, never as a profitability number. Prospecting and retargeting are never pooled: retargeting ROAS runs 4–7× against prospecting's 0.5–1.0×, so a blended figure just ranks pillars by how much retargeting they happened to receive. Any figure below $1,000 of spend inside one funnel is withheld as thin.

The verdict

one card per pillar · ranked by prospecting CTR, not by spend
Spend is the input; attention is the outcome — so the cards are ordered by how well each pillar earned a click from a cold audience. Click any card to open its sub-pillars and the individual creative concepts inside it. Prospecting shows impressions and reach; reach is the honest denominator for how many distinct people heard the message.

Primary × secondary message

for one primary pillar, how each secondary message did · follows the filters above
Many ads lead with one idea and carry another underneath — “Save 25%, best time ever to quit coffee” is offer-led with a Quitting Coffee secondary. Pick a primary pillar: each row is a secondary message tagged on its ads, plus a No secondary tagged row as the baseline. Prospecting and retargeting stay separate, and the $1,000 reliability gate applies inside each funnel: below it, CTR, ROAS and cost per purchase show n/a rather than a number that would rank on noise. ROAS is Meta-attributed, for ranking messages against each other — not a profit figure.

Google — campaign level

no creative read · no funnel split · never summed with Meta
Google is largely a product and intent channel, not a message channel. Campaign names carry a theme, but there is no per-ad creative data and PMax campaigns have no reliable funnel label — so there is no TOF/retargeting split here and these rows cannot be compared like-for-like with the Meta cards. The date filter applies here; the ad-type filter does not, because there is no creative record to read a type from. Data through 2026-11-13.

Tag guesses to check

AdSmith looked at each ad's pictures, headlines or video and made a best guess at its tags. A guess is not a tag: nothing on this page counts it until you act on it. Verify saves the guess as your tag (primary pillar and secondary messages) exactly as shown. Correct opens the tag picker with the guess filled in, so you change what is wrong and then save. Both save automatically and go through the same checks as any other tag, then count on this page within about 30 minutes. A guess can never replace a tag you have already confirmed. The Tagged now box shows how each ad is tagged today, so you can see where AdSmith disagrees. Tagging an ad does not approve what the ad says — any claim flag below still needs its own review. Spend shown is the full 12-month window; this list does not follow the date filter.

Untagged ads

the worklist behind the coverage figure · 54 ads · $17,856 over the full window
Every ad here is spend this page cannot read a message off. It is still inside every denominator above — nothing is dropped — but it contributes no signal to any pillar, so each dollar of it is a dollar we cannot learn from. The three reasons below need three different people to do three different things, which is why they are split rather than pooled into the single coverage figure. This panel follows the date and ad-type filters; the full-window backlog is restated beside the selection so narrowing can never make it look smaller than it is. Click any picture to open that ad on Creative Performance — full image, ad copy and Instagram link — so you can see what it says before you tag it.
Not one ad in this window is tagged from its own name — every tag on this page came from a hand-classified file. Ads are tagged after launch: pick tags above and they save automatically (from your private link). They are checked against the taxonomy and appear on this page and on Creative Performance within about 30 minutes. New ads land here untagged, so this list is the standing to-do — the last-30-day figure says how far behind it is.

No readable message signal. Still counted in every denominator on this page — unclassified spend never silently vanishes. The Untagged ads panel above names the 54 ads this is, split by what would have to happen to fix each one.

Ads split out of the IG Post* container names. Each is a different organic post sharing one ad name, so the tag is inherited, not verified. Split at ad level here so they are never treated as one comparable angle.

AdSmith recorded the evidence behind every tag; these are the calls made on the weakest evidence. The classification file itself marks $15,604 low — splitting the container names adds the rest, because an inherited tag is not a verified one.

Concept-level spend sitting in a funnel with under $1,000. Real money, but no CTR or ROAS is shown for it anywhere on this page.

Offer-led, no message
Holiday and discount ads whose organizing idea is the offer. Mail-merging a holiday into a fixed sentence is not a message, so tagging them by their boilerplate would inject fake signal.

PMax / Shopping / Feed-Only, where Google assembles the ad from the product feed and no message was ever chosen. Percentage is of Google spend, not Meta.

Branded search. People already looking for Teeccino — a high CTR here is not a message that persuaded anyone. Percentage is of Google spend.
Sources. Meta: raw_meta_ad_insights_daily (per-ad daily). Google: raw_google_ads_campaigns (per-campaign daily). Both in the analytics database, refreshed by the nightly pipeline.
Tags. Taxonomy v2 — the Pillars, ratified 2026-09-11 — the top axis is a Pillar and the second level a Sub-pillar; Caffeine Free was split out of Quitting Coffee. Content owned by AdSmith, schema by AgentSmith. Each ad is resolved from its own name first (per the ratified naming standard) and only then from the hand-classified concept file, so the page gets easier as the naming standard lands rather than staying manual forever.
Funnel. Derived from the campaign name first and the ad-set name only as a fallback — one ad set currently sits under both a COLD and a Retargeting campaign, so ad-set-only derivation mis-buckets spend.
Reach is summed across days. It is not a de-duplicated count of unique people over the whole period; a person reached in two different weeks is counted twice. Use it to compare pillars against each other, not as an audience size.
Meta totals (for the filter you have selected). $254,787 across 9 pillar buckets — prospecting $219,688, retargeting $35,099. Prospecting CTR averages 1.96% across the selection; the UNDERSPENT flag fires at 1.4× that on under 4% of prospecting spend, and is recomputed against the selection rather than against the year.
Creative type. Meta's own field on the ad. It is absent on a slice of daily rows, so a null is back-filled from the same ad's other days — ad id first, then ad name, both verified to carry no conflicting type in this window. Whatever is still null is reported as type not reported and never folded into Image.
